A_target.statement:
Let $V$ be an [[Definition:Affine Variety|affine variety]] over a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] $k$ and $p \in V$.
Let $\mathfrak m_p$ be the [[Definition:Maximal Ideal of Ring|maximal ideal]] of functions vanishing at $p$.
Then the [[Definition:Cotangent Space|cotangent space]] of $V$ at $p$ is:
:$T_p^* V \cong \mathfrak m_p / \mathfrak m_p^2$

B_source.statement:
Let $I$ be an [[Definition:Ideal of Ring|ideal]] of a [[Definition:Commutative Ring with Unity|commutative ring]] $R$.
Then $I / I^2$ is an $R / I$-[[Definition:Module|module]] recording $I$ modulo second-order terms.

substitutions.the ideal being collapsed: the maximal ideal of functions vanishing at the point
substitutions.the square of the ideal: products of two functions each vanishing at the point
substitutions.the quotient of the ideal by its square: the cotangent space at the point

derived.the surviving first-order information: the differential of a function at the point
derived.the vanishing of second-order terms: products of two vanishing functions have zero differential, by the product rule

validity_conditions: Functions in the square of the maximal ideal are sums of products of two functions vanishing at the point, so by the product rule their differentials vanish there.
Hence the differential map factors through the quotient, and the quotient is exactly the space of first-order behaviours at the point.
The identification of this quotient with the dual of the tangent space requires the point to be closed with residue field the base field; otherwise the correspondence needs modification.
proof_plan: Let $\mathfrak m_p = \set {f \in \map k V: \map f p = 0}$.

Define $d_p: \mathfrak m_p \to T_p^* V$ by $f \mapsto \map {\d f} p$.
For $f, g \in \mathfrak m_p$, the [[Product Rule for Derivatives|product rule]] gives:
:$\map {\d \paren {f g} } p = \map f p \map {\d g} p + \map g p \map {\d f} p = 0$
So $d_p$ vanishes on $\mathfrak m_p^2$.
Hence $d_p$ factors through the quotient $\mathfrak m_p / \mathfrak m_p^2$, which keeps only first-order information.

$d_p$ is [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]] as the coordinate functions $x_i - p_i$ map to a spanning set, and its kernel is exactly $\mathfrak m_p^2$ by [[Taylor's Theorem|Taylor expansion]].
Hence:
:$T_p^* V \cong \mathfrak m_p / \mathfrak m_p^2$
{{qed}}
